title: Smooth/regular-immersion interchange and section cancellation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work with separated finite-type compactifiable maps of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-asd-compactifiable]. Use ordinary small-etale derived categories and compact-support right adjoints [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For a regular closed immersion $i$ of codimension $c$, put $i^?=i^!(c)[2c]$ and write $a_i:\Lambda\to i^?\Lambda$ for its supported Kummer class [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. For a smooth map $q$ of dimension $r$, put $q^?=q^!(-r)[-2r]$ and write $a_q:\Lambda\to q^?\Lambda$ for the shifted diagonal/DNC orientation [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. Regular immersions and smooth maps mean [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. In formulas let $a_v\star a_u=u^?(a_v)\circ a_u$, using exceptional transitivity and the canonical twist identifications.

For a Cartesian square $Z'=Z\times_X X'$ with regular closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, smooth $q:X'\to X$, and projections $j:Z'\hookrightarrow X'$, $q':Z'\to Z$, one has
$$a_q\star a_j=a_i\star a_{q'}.$$
For a smooth map $q:V\to S$ with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, one has
$$a_q\star a_s=1_{\Lambda_S}.$$
These are equalities of the specified maps, including their Kummer signs, and hold over arbitrary Noetherian bases, not only bases smooth over a field.

source.place: Expose XVI, Lemmas 2.5.7 and 2.5.8 (the two identities), with the smooth orientation replaced by the diagonal/DNC normalization of lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality. Source proof uses a classical trace route; the replacement is justified by the diagonal/DNC coordinate normalization in Scholze Theorem 7.19 and the section-deformation comparison lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation. No classical trace theorem is taken as an input.

proof.text: Use $r$ for the smooth dimension and $c$ for the immersion codimension. Smooth base change preserves $r$, and smooth maps are flat. The flat-base-change clause of the regular-immersion class calculus therefore applies to $q$: $j$ is regular of codimension $c$ on nonempty components. Write $c_i:Ri_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$ for the transpose of $a_i$, and similarly $c_j$. Under closed-immersion exchange and Tate pullback this clause says $q^*c_i=c_j$, as supported maps. No regularity of the ambient schemes, excellence, or field hypothesis has been used.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.7: flat pullback of the supported class

proof.text: We identify the orientation of $p_d:P=\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ with the adjoint $\gamma'$ of the counit $t_{p_d}$ of the affine-space trace node; Steps 8–9 use this for $d=1$ over arbitrary Noetherian bases. Let $x$ be the coordinates of $P$, let $p_1:P\times_SP\to P$ be the first projection with fibre coordinates $y$, let $p_2$ be the second projection and $\Delta$ the diagonal. (i) Base change: the base-change clause of the affine-space trace, transposed through the counit formula for $\beta$ of the smooth base-change node as in Step 3, shows that $\beta\circ p_2^*\gamma'$ is the adjoint orientation of the coordinate-tower counit of $p_1$ in the coordinates $y$. (ii) Translation: $\tau_x:(x,y)\mapsto(x,y-x)$ is the $P$-automorphism of $\mathbf A^d_P$ given by the section $x$. The translation-trace node gives $t\circ Rp_{1!}(\kappa_x)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{\tau_x}=t$. Transposing, the adjoint orientations in the coordinates $y$ and $u=y-x$ agree under the etale comparison for $\tau_x$. (iii) Deformation: the smooth-duality node's inverse orientation is diagonal base change, then the deformation comparison $\delta_{p_1,\Delta}$, then the zero-section restriction of vector-bundle purity normalized by $t_qh=1$ and the ordered product, i.e. of the adjoint of the coordinate-tower counit. The coordinate clause of the section-deformation node applies to the chart $e=\tau_x$, with $e\Delta=0$ and $e^{-1}(0)=\Delta$ (here $p_1$ is compactifiable by Nagata). On this chart $\kappa$ is the identity of the pulled-back affine dualizing line, and the normal-bundle orientation is the section restriction of the adjoint orientation in the coordinates $u$; that node makes it frame-independent. Since $p_2\Delta=1$, (i)–(iii) give $\gamma_{p_d,\Lambda}=\gamma'$, with no free scalar. For $d=0$ all comparisons are identities.

source.place: Steps 3–4: diagonal deformation and the affine-space adjunction; ordinary finite-ring coordinate normalization

proof.text:
For a smooth $h$ of dimension $d$, put $T_hM=h^*M(d)[2d]$ and $t_{h,M}=\epsilon_{h,M}\circ Rh_!(\gamma_{h,M}):Rh_!T_hM\to M$. This is natural in $M$. For a base change $b$, denote compact-support exchange by $C:b^*Rh_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh'_!b'^*$. The exceptional comparison $\beta:b'^*h^!\to h'^!b^*$ is, by its counit-defined mate formula, characterized by
$$\epsilon_{h',b^*M}\circ Rh'_!\beta_M=b^*\epsilon_{h,M}\circ C^{-1}_{h^!M}.$$
The smooth orientation's base-change clause gives $\beta_M\circ b'^*\gamma_{h,M}=\gamma_{h',b^*M}$. Substitute this into the preceding formula and use naturality of $C$. The result is
$$t_{h',b^*M}\circ C_{T_hM}=b^*t_{h,M},$$
with the canonical pullback/twist comparison inserted. The identity and composite comparisons here are the compact-support comparisons; their mates paste by mate-pasting. Every application of compact-support exchange below is on bounded-below objects.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.7: replace the classical trace input by the counit-defined mate and diagonal/DNC base-change clause

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 with $h=q$, $b=i$, and $M=Ri_*\Lambda_Z$. Closed-immersion exchange gives $q^*M=Rj_*\Lambda_{Z'}$. The proper tensor projection formula for $j$ and Tate pullback identify $T_qM$ with $Rj_*\Lambda_{Z'}(r)[2r]$. Compact-support composition then identifies $Rq_!T_qM$ with $Ri_*Rq'_!\Lambda_{Z'}(r)[2r]$. Here closed pushforward equals compact-support pushforward, using its identity-open compactification. Also $i^*Ri_*\Lambda_Z=\Lambda_Z$. Thus Step 3 gives $i^*t_{q,M}=t_{q',\Lambda_Z}$ under these comparisons. To recover the supported map, closed direct image is fully faithful with exact left inverse $i^*$ on abelian sheaves; it is exact by the supported-kernel adjunction node. The same assertions hold for constant-$\Lambda$ modules: the maps and their inverses preserve scalar actions. Applying these exact adjoint functors to complexes and then localizing preserves their adjunction and its invertible counit. Hence $Ri_*$ is fully faithful and $i^*$ detects equality of maps between its image objects. Both endpoints of $t_{q,M}$ have the displayed form $Ri_*(-)$. It follows that
$$t_{q,Ri_*\Lambda_Z}=Ri_*t_{q',\Lambda_Z}.$$
The constants, twists, shifts, and exact closed direct images used here are bounded below; the source after $Rq'_!$ is bounded below by the compact-support theorem.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.7: identify the trace on a closed-supported input

proof.text:
Naturality of $t_{q,-}$ for $c_i:Ri_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$, together with Steps 1 and 4, gives
$$t_{q,\Lambda_X(c)[2c]}\circ Rq_!(c_j(r)[2r])=c_i\circ Ri_*t_{q',\Lambda_Z}.$$
Both sides map $R(qj)_!\Lambda_{Z'}(r)[2r]$ to $\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$. Transpose through $R(qj)_!\dashv(qj)^!$, using $qj=iq'$, and move the source twist $(r)[2r]$ to the target. The left transpose is $j^!(\gamma_{q,\Lambda})(c-r)[2(c-r)]\circ a_j$; the right transpose is $q'^!(a_i)(-r)[-2r]\circ a_{q'}$. The composite-adjunction Hom formula gives these two expressions by successive transposition; the smooth-duality tensor formula identifies the comparison at $\Lambda_X(c)[2c]$ with the corresponding twist of $\gamma_{q,\Lambda}$. They are precisely $a_q\star a_j$ and $a_i\star a_{q'}$. Their common target is $(qj)^!\Lambda_X(c-r)[2(c-r)]$. All shift interchanges are even, so no Koszul minus sign appears.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.7: explicitly transpose naturality through the two composite adjunctions

proof.text: For the section assertion let $q:V\to S$ be smooth of dimension $r$ with the given closed section $s$. The finite-ring section-deformation statement gives that $s$ is regular of codimension $r$. Its local coordinate model can also be chosen over Zariski neighbourhoods of points of $S$: apply smooth-pair local coordinates to $S\hookrightarrow V$ over $S$, with $S\to S$ the identity. Its coordinate subspace has relative dimension zero, hence $a=0$, and its ambient space has dimension $r$. After shrinking the base inside $s^{-1}(U)$, this gives an etale $S$-map $e:U\to\mathbf A^r_S$ with $es=0$ and $e^{-1}(0)=s(S)$ scheme-theoretically. One can choose affine base and source neighbourhoods; then $e$ is separated. All opens are Noetherian; the affine-space schemes are Noetherian by finite type. The separated finite-type maps and their composites are compactifiable by Nagata, since their Noetherian bases are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus all orientation, compact-support and interchange assertions can be applied to these charts. The existing section-deformation statement supplies exactly the same Cartesian-centre coordinate normalization.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.8: section charts without reduction to a field; Stacks 0FUE/lemma-etale-local-structure

proof.text: Compute over an arbitrary Noetherian base $T$ for $p_1:\mathbf A^1_T\to T$ and its zero section $z$. In the compactification $j:\mathbf A^1_T\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^1_T$, $v:P\to T$, put $\bar z=jz$. The divisor line bundle $\mathcal O_P(\bar z(T))$ is $\mathcal O_P(1)$: its ideal has local generators $t$ and $1$ on the standard charts, so its dual has the standard transition $t^{-1}$. The supported Kummer map $c_{\bar z}$ therefore satisfies $c_{\bar z}\circ u=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$, where $u:\Lambda_P\to R\bar z_*\Lambda_T$ is the unit. After $Rv_*$, precompose with the unit $\Lambda_T\to Rv_*\Lambda_P$. The composite to $Rv_*R\bar z_*\Lambda_T=\Lambda_T$ is the identity, by the composite-unit formula and $v\bar z=1_T$. Consequently $Rv_*c_{\bar z}$, under this identification of its source, is exactly the map $h:\Lambda_T\to Rv_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]$ in the projective-line adjunction. That adjunction's counit has $t_vh=1$.

source.place: XVI, Lemmas 2.5.9–2.5.10: Kummer first Chern class of the zero divisor and the normalized projective-line counit

proof.text: The supported Kummer map for $\bar z$ restricts to $c_z$ on $\mathbf A^1_T$. The affine-line adjunction is the composite of extension by zero/restriction for $j$ and the projective-line adjunction. Its composite-counit formula therefore identifies $t_{p_1}\circ Rp_{1!}c_z$ with $t_v\circ Rv_*c_{\bar z}=1$ from Step 7. By Step 2, $t_{p_1}$ is the transpose of the specified diagonal/DNC $\gamma_{p_1,\Lambda}$. Transposing this equality under the composite $p_1z=1_T$ identifies it with $a_{p_1}\star a_z=1_{\Lambda_T}$. The regular-immersion class calculus identifies $a_z$ with the transpose of this particular $c_z$, including its positive Kummer sign.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.9, rank one: restrict the projective-line adjunction and transpose its normalized evaluation

proof.text:
Induct on $d\geq0$ to prove $a_{p_d}\star a_{z_d}=1$ for the affine-space projection and zero section over every allowed base $T$. At $d=0$ the dimension-zero smooth comparison and the codimension-zero identity class are identities. For $d>0$, write $p_d=p_{d-1}\pi$ where $\pi:\mathbf A^d_T\to\mathbf A^{d-1}_T$ forgets the last coordinate, and $z_d=z'z_{d-1}$ where $z'$ is its zero section. The smooth composition clause gives $a_{p_d}=a_{p_{d-1}}\star a_\pi$. The regular-immersion composition clause, using the coordinate flag cutting the last coordinate first, gives $a_{z_d}=a_{z'}\star a_{z_{d-1}}$. The coherent composition comparisons and the composite-adjunction formula make $\star$ associative. Thus
$$a_{p_d}\star a_{z_d}=a_{p_{d-1}}\star(a_\pi\star a_{z'})\star a_{z_{d-1}}=a_{p_{d-1}}\star a_{z_{d-1}}=1.$$
The first cancellation is Step 8 over the Noetherian base $\mathbf A^{d-1}_T$; the second is the induction hypothesis. Only composition of smooth maps and of regular immersions has been used, not factorization independence for general maps.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.9: induction through the ordered affine coordinate tower

proof.text:
On a chart from Step 6 write $p_r:\mathbf A^r_S\to S$ and $q|_U=p_re$. Etale adjoint locality and the open-restriction clauses of both class nodes compute the original composite on this neighbourhood. Smooth composition and the dimension-zero normalization give $a_{q|_U}=a_{p_r}\star a_e$. Apply the already proved interchange identity (Steps 1–5) to the Cartesian square of $e$ over $z_r$: its lower immersion is $z_r$, its upper immersion is $s$, and its other smooth edge is $1_S$. It gives $a_e\star a_s=a_{z_r}\star a_{1_S}=a_{z_r}$. Hence associativity and Step 9 yield
$$a_q\star a_s=a_{p_r}\star a_e\star a_s=a_{p_r}\star a_{z_r}=1$$
on this base neighbourhood. Globally these are endomorphisms of $\Lambda_S[0]$. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero single-complex functor identifies them with sheaf maps; such a map is determined by the image of the unit, a section of $\Lambda_S$. Sections that agree on a Zariski cover agree globally. This proves the section identity over $S$, retaining the specified signs and without reducing the base to a field. Empty schemes give the unique maps, and the arguments include $r=0$ and $c=0$.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.5.8: etale chart reduction and gluing of degree-zero endomorphisms

proof_origin.place: XVI, Lemmas 2.5.7–2.5.10; explicit counit/mate calculation adapted to the stipulated diagonal/DNC prime-power orientation, using the current lecture-notes coordinate normalization instead of a classical trace theorem.
